title: Integrations: Forms, Portals, WhatsApp, Email and Payments

cards.body:
*Lesson 7.5 · Integrations: Forms, Portals, WhatsApp, Email and Payments*

_≈ 2.5 hours · with Miracle_

A CRM only stays true if information flows into it without anyone typing. For Kora that means: website forms and property-portal enquiries arrive as deals; WhatsApp conversations and emails attach to the right contact; an acknowledgement goes out in minutes; and when a buyer pays the holding deposit on Paystack, the deal moves and the accounts team knows. This lesson is the integration layer: what to connect natively, what to build in n8n, and how to keep it secure, idempotent and within every platform's limits.

*"The CRM is right only when Bisi updates it"*

*Week 2 after launch:* Portal enquiries arrive by email. Bisi, the administrator, retypes them into the CRM. When she's off, the CRM goes stale.

*Echo:* "Offers and promises live in twelve phones. When an agent leaves, so does the history."

*Glitch:* "I connected the website straight to the CRM. The private token is in the page's code, so it's quick!"

*Nodo:* "Everything flows in by itself, through one place we can watch. Secrets stay on the server."

*Native, marketplace app or middleware?*

_Connection · Best first choice · Why_
- *Website forms* · The CRM's own forms (embedded), or the form tool's native integration · Handles consent fields, tracking and duplicates out of the box
- *Gmail / Outlook* · Native inbox connection and logging · Emails attach to contacts automatically
- *Property portals (email alerts)* · n8n: parse the alert email, upsert · No native integration; the format is the portal's
- *WhatsApp Business* · A marketplace inbox app, or n8n with the Cloud API · Depends on budget and plan; both must follow WhatsApp's rules
- *Paystack* · n8n: verified webhook → CRM · Money events need signature checks and idempotency

- *Prefer native when it does the job*: Fewer moving parts, supported by the vendor, survives you. Use middleware when native doesn't exist, can't apply your rules, or would cost an expensive tier just for one feature.
- *Secrets live on the server*: Private app tokens, API keys and webhook secrets go in n8n credentials or environment variables, never in a web page, a spreadsheet or a WhatsApp message (Glitch's mistake).

*The upsert-enquiry pattern*

Every source (form, portal, Instagram, WhatsApp) calls one sub-workflow, so the rules live in one place. You built a version of this in 5.9; here it handles a paid CRM with custom objects and routing.
Code example on screen (The upsert-enquiry pattern): open it in the app.

- *Idempotent*: Running it twice with the same input changes nothing the second time. Portals resend; webhooks retry; people double-click. Without step 1, every retry creates a duplicate deal.
- *Rate limits and retries*: CRM APIs limit requests per second and per day; respect the vendor's published limits, batch where possible, and retry with a wait on "429 Too Many Requests" or 5xx errors.

*WhatsApp and email: history in the CRM, rules respected*

- *Business number, not personal phones*: To bring WhatsApp into the CRM, conversations must run through the business's WhatsApp Business Platform number (Cloud API or a provider), not agents' personal WhatsApp. Agree this change with the team early: it's the biggest adoption hurdle.
- *The 24-hour window and templates*: Free-form replies are allowed within 24 hours of the customer's last message. Outside it, only pre-approved templates (e.g. the enquiry acknowledgement, viewing reminders). Templates are charged per message; check Meta's current rates for Nigeria.
- *Opt-in*: Only message people who gave you their number for this purpose and agreed to WhatsApp contact; record it on the contact (the consent field from 7.2).
- *Email*: Connect each agent's inbox natively so sent and received emails log to the contact. Exclude private and personal mail by logging only to known contacts.
*Integration lab: safe or unsafe?*
Hands-on lab: Integration lab: safe or unsafe?. It's interactive, so open it in the app and try it there.

*Payments and monitoring*

- *Money moves deals, carefully*: A holding deposit or rent payment on Paystack can move a deal and notify accounts. Verify the webhook signature, confirm the transaction with Paystack's API, match it to the deal by a reference you created (not by name or amount), and store the Paystack reference on the deal. Never let a payment event close a deal as Won on its own if the business needs a signed contract first.
- *An integration log*: One table: time, source, event ID, result (created/updated/skipped/error), CRM IDs, error message. It answers "did the enquiry from Mrs X arrive?" in seconds.
- *Monitoring*: An error workflow alerts you on failures; a daily check compares counts (portal emails received vs. deals created); a weekly look at the API usage page. Tokens expire and portals change their email format: you want to know the same day, not when an agent complains.

cards.body:
*Solved problem: Kora's integration layer*

*The goal.* Website and portal enquiries become owned deals within 5 minutes without anyone typing; WhatsApp and email history sits on the contact; a deposit paid on Paystack moves the deal and tells accounts; every event is logged and failures alert the same day.

*Step 1 · KORA · Upsert enquiry (sub-workflow)*

Built once, as in Card 2, with a `kora_integration_log` table (Supabase or Google Sheets). Inputs validated; CRM calls via a private app token (scopes: contacts, deals, custom objects; nothing else) stored in n8n credentials.
*Step 2 · Sources*
Code example on screen (Sources): open it in the app.

*Step 3 · Acknowledge within minutes*

When routing (7.4) sets the owner, n8n sends the approved WhatsApp template _enquiryreceived_ ("Hi {{1}}, thanks for your enquiry about {{2}}. {{3}} from Kora will call you shortly.") if the contact gave a phone and WhatsApp consent; otherwise an email from the agent's address.

*Step 4 · Paystack deposit → deal*

_(Code on screen in the app.)_

*Step 5 · Monitor*

Error workflow → Telegram alert to you and the office manager. 7:00 daily check: portal emails received yesterday vs. deals created from portals; mismatch → alert. Monthly: token expiry dates and API usage in the register.

- *0* enquiries typed by hand
- *4 min* median enquiry → acknowledgement
- *1* place to look when something's missing

*Why this approach works*

- One upsert, many sources: rules in one place.
- Idempotent on event IDs, so retries are harmless.
- Secrets only on the server, with narrow scopes.
- Money events verified twice and matched by reference.
- A log and a daily count catch silent failures.

*Common mistakes to avoid*

- Tokens in browser code or shared sheets.
- Matching payments by name or amount.
- Letting a payment mark a deal Won.
- Messaging people outside WhatsApp's rules.
- No alert when a portal changes its email format.

*Glitch hunt*

*Glitch:* Everything's connected to everything. Isn't that the point?

*A:* A portal resent last week's alerts; 60 duplicate deals appeared.
*B:* A fake webhook call moved a deal to "Legal and payment" with no money received.
*C:* Since Tuesday, no portal enquiries have arrived in the CRM. Nobody noticed until Friday.
*D:* The integration's token had full admin scopes "in case we need them later".
*E:* A buyer's good email was replaced with a blank when they sent a WhatsApp from a new number.

cards.prompt: Made your call on each one? Tap Reveal to check.
cards.answer:
*A:* not idempotent. Store each source event ID and skip ones already processed.
*B:* no signature check and no server-side verification. Verify the HMAC and confirm the transaction with Paystack before moving anything.
*C:* the portal changed its email format and the parser silently failed. Alert on parse errors and compare daily counts.
*D:* excess privilege. Give tokens only the scopes they need; rotate on staff or contractor changes.
*E:* blind overwrite. Never replace a value with a blank; only fill gaps or update with verified newer data.

cards.title: Bronze (+25 XP): Draw the integration map
cards.body:
- For a business you know, list every source of customer information and decide native, marketplace app or middleware for each, with the reason and the security rule.

*Done when:*
- Every connection has a named owner, where its secret lives, and how failures are noticed.

cards.title: Silver (+50 XP): Build the upsert and two sources
cards.body:
- Build the upsert-enquiry sub-workflow against a trial CRM, plus a form webhook (with a secret) and an email parser.

*Done when:*
- Sending the same event three times creates one deal, the integration log shows all three, and a parse failure raises an alert.

cards.title: Gold (+100 XP): Payments and WhatsApp, end to end
cards.body:
- Add a Paystack test-mode deposit that moves a deal after verification, and a WhatsApp test-number acknowledgement template.

*Done when:*
- A forged webhook is rejected, a real test payment moves the right deal once, and the acknowledgement arrives on your phone.

options: Processing the same event twice changes nothing the second time
It uses the newest API version
cards.why: Store event IDs; skip ones you've already handled.

cards.q: Where should the CRM's private app token live?
options: In the server's credentials or environment variables
In a WhatsApp group for the team
cards.why: Secrets stay on the server, with only the scopes needed.

cards.q: A Paystack webhook says a deposit was paid. What do you do before moving the deal?
options: Verify the signature, confirm with Paystack's API, and match your own reference
cards.why: Money events are verified twice and matched by a reference you created.

cards.q: A buyer last messaged on WhatsApp three days ago. Can you send a free-form follow-up?
options: No; outside 24 hours only an approved template, to an opted-in contact
cards.why: WhatsApp's customer service window is 24 hours.

cards.q: How do you notice a silently broken portal parser?
options: Wait for an agent to complain
Alert on parse errors and compare daily counts of emails vs. deals
cards.why: Count-based checks catch failures that don't throw errors.

cards.body:
*Remember this*

1. Native where it does the job; middleware where it doesn't or where rules must apply.
2. One idempotent upsert sub-workflow for every source; never overwrite good data with blanks.
3. Secrets on the server with narrow scopes; webhooks verified.
4. WhatsApp through the business number, inside the 24-hour window or with templates, to opted-in contacts.
5. Payments verified twice and matched by reference; every integration logged and monitored.

*Lesson 7.5 complete!* _Integrations: Forms, Portals, WhatsApp, Email and Payments_ is done and saved to your progress, on WhatsApp and in the app.

Next up: Lesson 7.6, _Launch, Adoption and Reporting: Making the Team Use It_.
